slides.title: VibeAct: Vibration to Actions for Contact-Rich Reactive Robot Dexterity
slides.highlight: VibeAct uses piezoelectric microphones and a shared physical representation of contact and slip to bridge real vibrotactile sensing with simulation-based reinforcement learning. This framework improves success rates in contact-rich tasks like regrasping and insertion by providing rapid tactile feedback.

card.one_liner: VibeAct enables sim-to-real dexterous manipulation by bridging vibrotactile sensing and RL via shared contact representations.
card.key_idea: A tactile estimator maps real piezoelectric microphone signals to a compact contact/slip representation, which is also computed directly in simulation for RL policy training.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five contact-rich tasks (e.g., peg insertion) using PPO; outperformed proprioception+point-cloud baselines in simulation and real-world deployment.
card.limitation: Discards raw vibration details (texture, location), requires accurate object pose tracking for labeling, and is tied to specific hardware configurations.

slides.title: Self Capacitive Tactile Sensor System designed for Companion Robots
slides.tldr: SCALABLE TACTILE SENSING FOR COMPANION ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work presents a scalable, self-capacitance-based tactile sensing system using conductive fabric, supporting real-time interaction detection for companion robots. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A scalable, FPGA-based self-capacitive tactile sensing system for companion robots using conductive fabric electrodes.
card.key_idea: Uses a single conductive fabric layer and RC relaxation method for sensing, with a Decision Tree classifier implemented on an FPGA to offload real-time processing from the main CPU.
card.evaluation: Tested a 100-point array at 10, 100, and 1000 Hz; 100 Hz was optimal. Decision Tree achieved 90.4% accuracy for five interaction types.
card.limitation: Currently limited to 100 sensors and a small set of interaction gestures, insufficient for full-body coverage.

slides.title: NoContactNoWorries: Estimating Contact through Vision and Proprioception for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work presents a transformer-based multimodal framework that fuses RGB-D vision and proprioception to infer contact states, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A transformer-based framework that infers binary fingertip contact using only RGB-D vision and robot proprioception.
card.key_idea: Fuses RGB-D tokens with current and commanded joint configurations via pose-conditioned cross-attention and a causal transformer for temporal reasoning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LEAP hand in simulation and real-world using F1 scores and in-hand reorientation tasks; results show robust generalization to novel objects.
card.limitation: Performance degrades on real-world hardware due to sensing noise and high visual occlusion with non-convex geometries.

slides.title: Bridging Handheld and Teleoperated Supervision for Contact-Rich Manipulation via State-Gated Experts
slides.tldr: HYBRID DATA COLLECTION FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces BRIDGE, a mixture of diffusion policy experts that combines scalable handheld data with targeted teleoperated demonstrations to improve success rates in contact-sensitive tasks.

card.one_liner: BRIDGE improves contact-rich manipulation by routing between handheld-observed and teleoperated-desired action experts based on robot state.
card.key_idea: A mixture-of-diffusion-experts architecture using a state-conditioned MLP router to switch between a base policy (observed actions) and a support head (desired actions).
card.evaluation: Tested on three contact-rich tasks (pulley, pipe, battery insertion) against handheld and naive-mix baselines; success rates improved by up to 36.7%.
card.limitation: Hard-switching causes control discontinuities; identifying support phases is currently empirical and may scale poorly to long-horizon tasks.

slides.title: PhysReflect-VLA: Physical Feasibility and Self-Reflective Regulation for Reliable Vision-Language-Action Policies
slides.tldr: SELF-REFLECTIVE VLA FRAMEWORK FOR ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that uses physical feasibility evaluation and an LLM-based reflection module to diagnose execution errors and generate corrective guidance, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: PhysReflect-VLA enhances VLA policies with real-time physical feasibility checks and self-reflective error correction for reliable manipulation.
card.key_idea: A plug-and-play framework using a bidirectional consistency model (forward/inverse operators) to filter infeasible actions and an LLM-based reflection module for corrective guidance.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five real-robot long-horizon tasks against baselines like OpenVLA; showed an average success rate gain of 5.4%.

slides.title: LIBERO-Safety: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Physical and Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.highlight: This work introduces a parametric safety benchmark and a large-scale dataset to evaluate physical and semantic safety in Vision-Language-Action models, supporting the development of reliable embodied AI for RwB.

card.one_liner: LIBERO-Safety is a comprehensive benchmark evaluating physical and semantic safety in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.
card.key_idea: A parametric framework using UBDDL for procedural scene generation and a keypose-driven pipeline to synthesize 19,664 collision-free demonstrations for training and evaluating VLA safety.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 8 VLA and 2 foundation models across 75 tasks. Metrics include Success Rate, Collision Rate, and Refusal Rate; results show significant L2-tier vulnerabilities.
card.limitation: Task success is bottlenecked by sub-optimal trajectory synthesis and semantic misalignment, even when physical safety constraints are maintained.

slides.title: Learning to Fold: prizewinning solution at LeHome Challenge 2026
slides.tldr: BIMANUAL GARMENT FOLDING VIA VLA AND RL
slides.highlight: This work presents a vision-language-action (VLA) policy enhanced by a reinforcement-learning loop for bimanual garment folding, achieving top rankings in both simulation and real-world settings.

card.one_liner: A VLA-based bimanual garment folding system using RL and advantage conditioning to win the LeHome 2026 Challenge.
card.key_idea: Combines AWR and RECAP-style advantage conditioning with a VLA policy that acts as its own value function via auxiliary heads.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in Isaac Sim (1st/62 teams, 79.63% success) and a real-world final (2nd place) using geometric keypoint conditions.
card.limitation: Engineering case study lacking formal ablations; limited autonomous exploration/recovery and high reliance on simulation-to-real tuning.

slides.title: WOLF-VLA: Whole-Body Humanoid Optimal Locomotion Framework for Vision-Language-Action Learning
slides.highlight: This work introduces WOLF-VLA, a framework that enables humanoid robots to generate whole-body locomotion policies from natural-language instructions, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for training humanoid VLAs using optimal-control generated trajectories for dynamically consistent whole-body locomotion.
card.key_idea: Integrates a large-scale dataset of OC-synthesized, physically optimal humanoid trajectories with a transformer-based VLA model using flow-matching for action prediction.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six locomotion tasks (e.g., stair climbing) in MuJoCo; outperformed ACT and π0.5 baselines in success rate and ROM error.
card.limitation: Performance decreases for complex tasks (like walking around) as horizon length increases or visual distractors are introduced.
